name: ISO/IEC 42001 AI Management System (eucomplyhub)
description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI Management System (AIMS) starter framework for mid-market SaaS. Operationalizes AI governance ahead of the August 2, 2026 EU AI Act Article 50 enforcement deadline. Maintained by eucomplyhub.com.

framework.name: ISO/IEC 42001 AI Management System (eucomplyhub)
framework.description: Starter framework for implementing ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI Management System. Maps key management clauses (4-10) and Annex A AI controls. Designed for mid-market SaaS preparing for triple-framework alignment (EU AI Act + ISO 42001 + NIST AI RMF).

structure.title: Clause 4 Context of the Organization
structure.description: Understanding internal and external issues relevant to AI management, interested parties, AIMS scope, and the AI management system itself.

items.title: 4.1 Understanding the organization and its context
items.description: Determine internal and external issues affecting AIMS outcomes including AI system roles (provider, deployer, distributor) and applicable regulatory regimes (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, sectoral rules).
items.summary: Document organizational AI context + role + regulatory exposure
questions: What AI roles does the organization perform (provider, deployer, distributor, importer)?
Which jurisdictions and regulatory frameworks apply (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, sectoral)?
What internal/external issues affect AIMS outcomes?
Is the organizational AI strategy documented?
evidence_examples: Provider/deployer role determination per AI system

items.title: 4.2 Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties
items.description: Identify interested parties (users, customers, regulators, employees, third parties) and their AI-related requirements.
items.summary: Map AI stakeholders and their requirements
questions: Who are the interested parties for the AI systems?
What are their documented AI-related requirements?
How are conflicting stakeholder interests resolved?

items.title: 4.3 Scope of the AIMS
items.description: Define and document AIMS scope including AI systems in scope, boundaries, and exclusions with justification.
items.summary: Document AIMS scope statement with AI system inventory
questions: Is the AIMS scope statement documented?
Are AI systems in scope inventoried?
Are exclusions justified?

items.title: 4.4 AI Management System
items.description: Establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve the AIMS including required processes and their interactions.
items.summary: Establish AIMS with documented processes
questions: Is the AIMS structure documented?
Are AIMS processes and interactions mapped?
Is there a continual improvement mechanism?

structure.title: Clause 5 Leadership
structure.description: Top management commitment, AI policy, and roles, responsibilities, and authorities.

items.title: 5.1 Leadership and commitment
items.description: Top management demonstrates leadership and commitment by ensuring AI policy and objectives are established, AIMS requirements are integrated, and resources are available.
items.summary: Document top management AI commitment
questions: How does top management demonstrate AIMS commitment?
Are AI objectives integrated with business strategy?
Are adequate AI governance resources allocated?

items.title: 5.2 AI Policy
items.description: Establish, implement, and maintain an AI policy aligned with organizational strategic direction including commitment to responsible AI and continual improvement.
items.summary: Documented AI policy with responsible AI principles
questions: Is the AI policy documented and communicated?
Does the policy cover responsible AI principles?
Are policy review cycles defined?

items.title: 5.3 Roles, responsibilities, and authorities
items.description: Assign and communicate responsibilities and authorities for AIMS roles including AI risk owners, AI ethics officers, and Article 14 human oversight roles where applicable.
items.summary: RACI for AI governance roles including Article 14 oversight
questions: Are AI governance roles documented (RACI)?
Is there a named AI risk owner?
Are Article 14 human oversight roles assigned per AI system?

structure.title: Clause 6 Planning
structure.description: Actions to address AI risks and opportunities, AI objectives, planning AI changes, and AI impact assessment.

items.title: 6.1.2 AI risk assessment
items.description: Define and apply an AI risk assessment process covering risks to individuals, groups, and society. Maps directly to NIST AI RMF MAP function and EU AI Act Article 9 risk management.
items.summary: AI risk assessment process aligned with EU AI Act Art. 9 + NIST RMF MAP
questions: Is an AI risk assessment process documented?
Are risks to fundamental rights, safety, and fairness considered?
Does the process align with EU AI Act Article 9 and NIST AI RMF MAP?
Are risk acceptance criteria defined?
evidence_examples: Triple-framework crosswalk (EU AI Act Art. 9 + ISO 42001 6.1.2 + NIST RMF MAP)

items.title: 6.1.3 AI risk treatment
items.description: Select and apply AI risk treatment options. Document residual risk acceptance. Implement Annex A controls as applicable.
items.summary: AI risk treatment plan with Annex A control selection
questions: Is the AI risk treatment plan documented?
Are Annex A controls selected with justification (Statement of Applicability)?
Is residual risk accepted by risk owners?

items.title: 6.1.4 AI system impact assessment
items.description: Conduct AI system impact assessment covering individuals, groups, and society. For EU AI Act high-risk systems, aligns with Article 27 Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) for public-sector and creditworthiness/insurance deployers.
items.summary: AI impact assessment + FRIA where Article 27 applies
questions: Is the AI impact assessment process documented?
For EU AI Act high-risk systems, has FRIA been conducted where Article 27 applies?
Are impacts to vulnerable groups considered?

items.title: 6.2 AI objectives and planning
items.description: Establish measurable AI objectives at relevant functions and levels with planning, resources, responsibilities, and evaluation methods.
items.summary: SMART AI objectives with measurement plan
questions: Are AI objectives documented and measurable?
Is the planning aligned with risk treatment?
Are KPIs defined and tracked?

structure.title: Clause 7 Support
structure.description: Resources, competence, awareness, communication, and documented information for the AIMS.

items.title: 7.2 Competence
items.description: Determine necessary competence for persons affecting AI performance. Maintain training records. Includes AI literacy obligations under EU AI Act Article 4.
items.summary: AI competence + Article 4 AI literacy
questions: Are required AI competencies documented?
Is Article 4 AI literacy training delivered to staff working with AI?
Are training records maintained?

items.title: 7.5 Documented information
items.description: Create, update, and control documented information needed for the AIMS including Annex IV technical documentation for EU AI Act high-risk systems.
items.summary: Documented information control + Annex IV docs
questions: Is documented information control procedure in place?
For EU AI Act high-risk systems, is Annex IV technical documentation maintained?
Is documentation version-controlled?

structure.title: Clause 8 Operation
structure.description: Operational planning and control, AI risk assessment performance, AI risk treatment implementation, AI impact assessment performance.

items.title: 8.1 Operational planning and control
items.description: Plan, implement, and control processes needed to meet AIMS requirements including outsourced AI processes (third-party AI vendors).
items.summary: AI operational control including vendor management
questions: Are AI operational processes documented?
Are third-party AI vendors managed under AIMS?
Are changes to AI systems controlled?

items.title: 8.2 AI risk assessment performance
items.description: Perform AI risk assessment at planned intervals and when significant changes occur. Maintain documented information.
items.summary: Periodic + trigger-based AI risk assessments
questions: Are AI risk assessments conducted on schedule?
Are reassessments triggered by significant changes?
Are results documented?

items.title: 8.4 AI system impact assessment performance
items.description: Perform AI system impact assessment at planned intervals. For high-risk EU AI Act systems, maintain Article 26(6) post-market monitoring evidence.
items.summary: Impact assessments + Art. 26(6) post-market monitoring
questions: Are AI impact assessments performed periodically?
For EU AI Act high-risk systems, is Article 26(6) post-market monitoring evidence collected?
Are findings reported to management?

structure.title: Clause 9 Performance Evaluation
structure.description: Monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation, internal audit, and management review.

items.title: 9.1 Monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation
items.description: Determine what to monitor, methods, and when. Includes Article 15 accuracy/robustness monitoring and Article 50 transparency compliance metrics.
items.summary: AI performance monitoring + Art. 15 + Art. 50 metrics
questions: Are AI monitoring metrics defined?
Is Article 15 accuracy/robustness performance tracked?
Is Article 50 transparency compliance measured?

items.title: 9.2 Internal audit
items.description: Conduct internal AIMS audits at planned intervals. Maintain audit program, criteria, and records.
items.summary: AIMS internal audit program
questions: Is the internal AIMS audit program documented?
Are auditors competent and independent?
Are audit results reported to management?

items.title: 9.3 Management review
items.description: Top management reviews the AIMS at planned intervals to ensure suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
items.summary: Periodic AIMS management review
questions: Are management reviews conducted on schedule?
Do reviews cover required inputs (audits, risks, objectives, opportunities)?
Are decisions documented and tracked?

structure.title: Clause 10 Improvement
structure.description: Nonconformity, corrective action, and continual improvement of the AIMS.

items.title: 10.1 Continual improvement
items.description: Continually improve AIMS suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness.
items.summary: Continual AIMS improvement
questions: Are improvement opportunities identified systematically?
Are improvements implemented and tracked?
Is effectiveness of improvements measured?

items.title: 10.2 Nonconformity and corrective action
items.description: When nonconformity occurs, react, evaluate need for action, implement, review effectiveness, and update AIMS as needed.
items.summary: Nonconformity + CAPA process
questions: Is the nonconformity process documented?
Are corrective actions tracked to closure?
Is effectiveness of corrective actions verified?

structure.title: Annex A — AI Controls (Selected)
structure.description: Reference AI control objectives and controls. Selection of representative controls; full Statement of Applicability covers all 38 Annex A controls.

items.title: A.2.2 AI policy
items.description: Define and document the organization's AI policy including responsible AI principles, risk appetite, and roles.
items.summary: Documented AI policy with responsible AI principles
questions: Is the AI policy documented?
Does it address responsible AI principles?
Is the policy approved by management?

items.title: A.3.2 AI roles and responsibilities
items.description: Define, document, and assign AI-related roles and responsibilities across the AI lifecycle.
items.summary: AI lifecycle role assignment
questions: Are AI roles defined across lifecycle stages?
Is there a documented assignment matrix?
Are roles communicated to assigned personnel?

items.title: A.6.2.2 AI impact assessment
items.description: Conduct impact assessment of AI systems on individuals, groups, and society throughout the lifecycle.
items.summary: Lifecycle AI impact assessment
questions: Are impact assessments performed before deployment?
Are assessments repeated at significant changes?
Are vulnerable groups specifically considered?

items.title: A.7.4 Data quality for AI systems
items.description: Ensure data used for AI system development and operation meets quality criteria including representativeness, accuracy, and bias mitigation. Aligns with EU AI Act Article 10.
items.summary: Data quality + Art. 10 bias mitigation
questions: Are data quality criteria defined?
Is Article 10 data governance documented?
Are bias detection and mitigation procedures in place?

items.title: A.8.2 System and computing resources documentation
items.description: Document AI system architecture, computing resources, and dependencies including model cards and data sheets.
items.summary: AI system architecture documentation + model cards
questions: Are AI system architectures documented?
Are model cards maintained?
Are data sheets created for training datasets?

items.title: A.9.2 Information for interested parties (transparency)
items.description: Provide appropriate information to interested parties about the AI system. Maps directly to EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations.
items.summary: Transparency disclosure + EU AI Act Art. 50
questions: Are users informed when interacting with AI?
Is AI-generated content labeled per Article 50?
Are downstream deployers provided required information?

items.title: A.9.3 External reporting
items.description: Report on AI system performance, incidents, and impacts to external stakeholders as required. Includes EU AI Act Article 73 serious incident reporting.
items.summary: External reporting + Art. 73 incident reporting
questions: Is external reporting procedure documented?
Are Article 73 serious incident reports submitted within deadlines?
Are stakeholder reports timely and accurate?

items.title: A.10.2 Human oversight
items.description: Ensure appropriate human oversight of AI systems throughout the lifecycle. Maps directly to EU AI Act Article 14 human oversight requirements.
items.summary: Human oversight + EU AI Act Art. 14
questions: Are human oversight measures defined per AI system?
For EU AI Act high-risk systems, are Article 14 oversight conditions implemented?
Are override mechanisms tested?
